\chapter*{Pronunciation --- a reference, not a chapter}
\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{Pronunciation (reference)}
\markboth{Pronunciation}{Pronunciation}

A \textbf{reference}, not a chapter. Each lesson tells you the sounds you need for its word and links here for more. French spelling hides more sound than Spanish does — silent letters, nasal vowels, liaison — so this page is worth dipping into, but never a gate to pass before Lesson 1.

Ids (e.g. \texttt{silent-final}) are cited in each lesson's frontmatter \texttt{sounds:} field.

\section*{The big three habits (unlearn Spanish/English here)}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
\setlength{\itemsep}{0.35em}
  \item \texttt{silent-final} — \textbf{most final consonants are silent.} \emph{salut} $\to$ \emph{sa-LU} (no \emph{t}); \emph{vous} $\to$ \emph{voo} and \emph{les} $\to$ \emph{lay} (no \emph{s}). Common exceptions kept: final \emph{c, r, f, l} (the word \textquotedblleft{}CaReFuL\textquotedblright{}). \emph{bonjour}'s \emph{r} is pronounced.
  \item \texttt{liaison} — a normally-silent final consonant \textbf{reconnects} onto a following vowel: \emph{vous} + \emph{avez} $\to$ \emph{vou-zavez}. Comes later; just know it exists.
  \item \texttt{nasal} — some vowels are \textbf{nasal}: air through the nose, and the \emph{n}/\emph{m} itself goes silent. \emph{bon} is not \textquotedblleft{}bon\textquotedblright{} but a nasal \emph{bõ}; \emph{bien} is a nasal \emph{byẽ}. See below.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Vowels}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
\setlength{\itemsep}{0.35em}
  \item \texttt{vowel-ou} — \textbf{ou} = \emph{oo} as in \emph{food}: \emph{jour} (\emph{zhoor}), \emph{vous}, \emph{bonjour}.
  \item \texttt{vowel-u} — \textbf{u} = a front-rounded \emph{ee} with rounded lips (say \emph{ee}, then purse your lips): \emph{salut}, \emph{tu}. No English equivalent; not \emph{oo}.
  \item \texttt{vowel-oi} — \textbf{oi} = \emph{wa}: \emph{soir} (\emph{swahr}), \emph{bonsoir}, \emph{moi} (\emph{mwah}).
  \item \texttt{vowel-e-acute} — \textbf{é} = a crisp \emph{ay} (no glide): \emph{enchanté}.
  \item \texttt{vowel-e-grave} — \textbf{è / ê} = an open \emph{eh} as in \emph{bed}: \emph{très}.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Nasal vowels}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
\setlength{\itemsep}{0.35em}
  \item \texttt{nasal-on} — \textbf{on / om} = nasal \emph{õ} (like \emph{song} without the \emph{g}): \emph{bon}, \emph{bonjour}, \emph{bonsoir}, \emph{nom}.
  \item \texttt{nasal-in} — \textbf{in / ain / ien} = nasal \emph{ẽ}: \emph{bien} (\emph{byẽ}), \emph{matin}, \emph{bientôt}.
  \item \texttt{nasal-an} — \textbf{an / en} = nasal \emph{ã}: \emph{enchanté} (\emph{ã-shã-TAY}), \emph{comment}.
  \item \texttt{double-n-blocks-nasal} — a doubled \emph{nn}/\emph{mm} \textbf{cancels} the nasal and the vowel goes back through the mouth: \emph{bon} (\emph{bõ}) vs. \emph{bonne} (\emph{bun}).
\end{itemize}

\section*{Consonants that differ}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
\setlength{\itemsep}{0.35em}
  \item \texttt{j-zh} — \textbf{j} = the soft \emph{zh} of \emph{measure}: \emph{jour} (\emph{zhoor}), \emph{je} (\emph{zhuh}).
  \item \texttt{soft-g} — \textbf{g} before \emph{e/i} = the same \emph{zh}: \emph{âge}.
  \item \texttt{r-uvular} — \textbf{r} = a soft guttural sound at the back of the throat, not the Spanish tap/trill nor the English \emph{r}. \emph{bonjour}, \emph{soir}.
  \item \texttt{h-silent} — \textbf{h} is always silent (as in Spanish): \emph{heure} $\to$ \emph{euhr}.
  \item \texttt{ch-sh} — \textbf{ch} = English \emph{sh}: \emph{enchanté} (\emph{ã-\textbf{sh}ã-tay}).
  \item \texttt{gn} — \textbf{gn} = the \emph{ny} of \emph{canyon} (= Spanish \emph{ñ}): \emph{signe}.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Accents \& spelling marks}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
\setlength{\itemsep}{0.35em}
  \item \texttt{accent-marks} — French accents mostly change \textbf{vowel quality}, not stress: \emph{é} (closed \emph{ay}), \emph{è/ê} (open \emph{eh}), \emph{à/ù} (distinguish words), \emph{ç} (soft \emph{s}). Unlike Spanish, they do \textbf{not} mark which syllable is stressed — French stresses the \textbf{last} syllable of a group, lightly and evenly.
\end{itemize}
